overview: This bill would repeal a requirement, created by section 1071 of the 2010 Dodd-Frank financial reform law, that lenders collect and report data on loan applications from small businesses, including businesses owned by women and minorities. That data rule is carried out by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, a federal agency that oversees consumer finance. The bill deletes the requirement from the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the main federal law against lending discrimination, along with related references. It would affect banks, credit unions, and other lenders, as well as small business owners who seek credit. As of May 6, 2025, the House Financial Services Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say the reporting rule piles compliance costs on lenders, especially community banks and credit unions, which could lead them to make fewer small business loans.
against: Critics say the data is needed to spot unfair lending to women- and minority-owned businesses, and repealing it would leave regulators and the public unable to see whether small businesses are treated fairly.
